name: Lateral meniscus — body
description: Middle third of the lateral meniscus, between the anterior horn and the popliteal hiatus, with no LCL attachment. A low-signal triangle on coronal images and the bow tie on peripheral sagittal images; coronal images show its width.

normal_values.body_width_mid_coronal: about 11 mm; 15 mm or more is discoid
normal_values.bow_tie_sagittal_images: 2 consecutive images on 4–5 mm slices; the count does not carry over to 3 mm or 3D

variants_pitfalls: Discoid lateral meniscus (about 3–5% Western, 10–15% Asian, often bilateral): call it at 15 mm or more mid-coronal; spanning more than half the plateau width is a commonly used adult criterion. Discoid menisci tear easily.
The Wrisberg-type discoid can look normal in shape but lacks posterior capsular attachments, so the posterior horn can flip forward and mimic a bucket-handle tear.

Fewer bow ties than expected should send you looking for a displaced fragment, but it is non-specific (small or degenerated menisci, prior meniscectomy; positive predictive value 76% in one series). Base the call on the fragment.
Radial tears are most frequent here: a blunted free edge on coronal images and a cleft or missing triangle on one or two sagittal images.
